sections.h2: Which Redwood County offices deal with your tax bill?
sections.html:
Everything runs through the Redwood County Government Center at 403 South Mill Street in Redwood Falls. Valuation and classification belong to the Assessor, reached at 507-637-4008, and Jesse Jacobson holds that post. Billing and collection belong to the Auditor-Treasurer, Jean Price, at 507-637-4013. The Recorder, Amy Gewerth, files deeds at 507-637-4032.

Letters go to P.O. Box 130, Redwood Falls, MN 56283. Phone lines at the assessor's desk stay open weekdays until 4:30 p.m.

sections.h2: What is the housing market like in Redwood County?
sections.html:
Redwood County spreads across 882 square miles of rolling cropland in southwest Minnesota. The Minnesota River marks its northeastern border, the Redwood River runs east through the upper part, and the Cottonwood River crosses the lower part. The ground slopes eastward from a high point of 1,450 feet in the southwest corner. Lawmakers carved out the county in 1862 and took its name from the Redwood River.

Redwood Falls, the seat, had 5,102 residents in 2020 and joined with North Redwood in 1996. U.S. Highway 71 runs through it, joined by highways 19 and 67. Fourteen smaller cities share the county: Belview, Clements, Delhi, Lamberton, Lucan, Milroy, Morgan, Revere, Sanborn, Seaforth, Vesta, Wabasso, Walnut Grove and Wanda. The Lower Sioux Indian Reservation lies entirely inside the county, in Paxton and Sherman townships.

Redwood Falls grew from a claim staked in 1864 by Samuel McPhail, who donated land for the courthouse in 1872 when the town became the seat. John Honner built a house in North Redwood in 1869 that still stands and carries a federal historic listing. The city took over Alexander Ramsey Park from the state in 1958, and it is the largest municipal park in Minnesota.

Housing figures from Census Bureau QuickFacts:

  • 15,265 people in July 2025, which is 1.0% fewer than the 2020 base count.
  • A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $158,200 (2020 to 2024 figures).
  • Owners live in 78.4% of homes, and renters pay a median of $757 a month.
  • Seven building permits in all of 2025, and 7,133 housing units counted.

The 2020 census counted 7,086 housing units, with 10.8% vacant and 21.4% of occupied homes rented, and 70.1% of residents lived in rural areas. The county shares borders with Renville, Brown, Cottonwood, Murray, Lyon and Yellow Medicine Counties. At these prices, even a modest balance of back tax or penalty is a real line item on a closing statement.

sections.h2: When are Redwood County property taxes due in 2026?
sections.html:
Real estate tax comes due in mid-May and mid-October, and both of those 2026 dates are behind us. One deadline remains this year, tomorrow: agricultural land and manufactured homes owe the second half on Monday, November 16.

Redwood County 2026 property tax due dates, from the Auditor/Treasurer page
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estateFriday, May 15Thursday, October 15
Agricultural real estateFriday, May 15Monday, November 16
Personal propertyFriday, May 15None
Manufactured homeMonday, August 31Monday, November 16

Late payment penalties come from Minnesota Statutes section 279.01 and differ for homestead and nonhomestead land. The county also bills $30 for any bounced check, failed electronic payment or reversed payment.

sections.h2: What payment options does the Redwood County Auditor-Treasurer offer?
sections.html:
The county has an online payments page with a tax parcel lookup, and the Government Center accepts payments over the counter or through the post. A Direct Payment Plan pulls the amount from your checking or savings account, either twice a year or in one annual draft. Call 507-637-4013 to enroll.

Escrow customers should still read the statement. Before closing, request a payoff figure for the parcel from the same office, which also publishes the yearly delinquent tax list and notices of forfeited property sales and sales with unclaimed surplus.

sections.h2: How does the Redwood County assessor arrive at your value?
sections.html:
Every parcel gets a classification based on how it is used and an estimated market value fixed as of January 2. Appraisers walk each property on a five year cycle under Minnesota Statutes section 273.01, and tax-exempt parcels on a six year cycle. A new addition can bring an earlier visit.

The annual notice in spring shows that value and class, and it sets the tax for the following year. Details that affect homestead treatment:

  • On January 2 or December 1, the owner or a qualifying relative has to be living there.
  • The application deadline is December 31 of the assessment year, filed with the Assessor.
  • People who are blind or permanently disabled may apply for a separate class.
  • The disabled veterans' homestead exclusion form and special agricultural homestead forms come from the Assessor's office.

sections.h2: What is the process for contesting a Redwood County valuation?
sections.html:
Start by phoning the assessor about the notice. Failing that, the next stop is the local board of appeal and equalization for your city or township. The Assessor's office hosts those meetings in April, and the 2024 round ran from April 8 to April 24. In most cases you must be heard locally before your case can reach the commissioners.

The county board met on June 16, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in the Commissioner's Room. Its agenda that evening was one parcel, and the commissioners voted unanimously to deny the change. Beyond the boards, a petition to district court or Tax Court under section 278.01 is the last route, and it has an April 30 filing date.

sections.h2: What if Redwood County tax is unpaid when you want to sell?
sections.html:
Tax still open in early January turns delinquent under section 279.02, with an extra 2% added right away. The tax matters at closing for a second reason: the auditor must mark a deed with a no-delinquent-tax note before the Recorder accepts it under section 272.12. Probate distribution deeds and transfer on death deeds are among the listed exceptions.

In practice the title agent subtracts what you owe from your proceeds, so a quick call to the Auditor-Treasurer keeps surprises out of the closing statement.

sections.h2: Which Redwood County recording tools help before a sale?
sections.html:
The Recorder's page describes three. LandShark is a web tool for searching land records and viewing document images, and an account needs a signed web portal agreement with an original wet signature plus a set-up fee. Land Notification emails you when anything is filed against your personal or business name, so a surprise lien shows up quickly. The eCRV tool is where the sale certificate gets filed, and the county says paper certificates have not been accepted for sales since October 1, 2014.

After closing, the assessor drops homestead classification on the sold property for the next assessment year unless the buyer applies and qualifies, per section 272.115.

faqs.q: What is the last Redwood County tax deadline of 2026?
faqs.a: Monday, November 16, 2026, covering the second half on agricultural property and manufactured homes. Standard real estate second halves came due October 15.

faqs.q: Who can I call about a Redwood County home value I think is too high?
faqs.a: Call the County Assessor at 507-637-4008. If the answer does not satisfy you, the next steps are the local board in April and the county board in June.

faqs.q: Can a Redwood County house be sold with property tax still owing?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance has to be cleared before the Recorder will file the deed, and it normally comes out of the seller's proceeds. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-637-4013 for the exact payoff.

faqs.q: What is the Redwood County homestead application deadline?
faqs.a: December 31 of the assessment year. The home must be owned and occupied by the owner or a qualifying relative as of January 2 or December 1.

faqs.q: Will the buyer automatically get my Redwood County homestead status?
faqs.a: No. After a transfer the assessor removes homestead for the following assessment year unless the new owner files an application and qualifies.
